fix-round: gate findings on restack work (inc span, store race, ADR 0004, docs)
- _incremental_entries: a later uncovered commit now wins only a path's TIP
  side; old_oid/inc_parent stay the first uncovered touch's, so the
  incremental diff spans first uncovered parent -> tip blob and shows every
  uncovered commit's change to the file, not just the last one's
  (regression: test_two_uncovered_commits_same_file_full_span, both the
  blob-pair and the committing-range branches)
- rg_store.records_for_remote: a record vanishing between glob and read
  (_load_verdict_at -> None on FileNotFoundError, not StoreError) is skipped
  instead of landing None in the join's scan output
  (regression: test_records_for_remote_skips_records_that_vanish_mid_scan)
- ADR 0004 records the two new config surfaces: OCR_COVERAGE_V1 (coverage
  rollback switch) and --reset-tip (operator command), statuses accepted
- README: failed-run paragraph now describes retry (3 attempts) ->
  exhausted -> --reset-tip, replacing the stale sticky-error/doctor text
- ReviewGateError docstring points only at the module header's fail-open
  enumeration (ADR 0002/0003 never enumerated them)

fix(review): protocol v2 pins + docs_gate resolution interplay
A linear extension (a push whose covered commits keep their SHAs: some
joinable record's tip is an ancestor of the new tip) is the ordinary
fix-push, not a restack. restack-b's incremental path swallowed it and
skipped the resolver call entirely (_no_evidence), so the prior doc
finding judged 'unverified' and a fixed push re-blocked forever -- the
resolver is the only clearing path and must still run over the union
(spec: Incremental review and verdict combination). True restacks
(rewritten SHAs) keep the never-spend-a-resolver-call behaviour.

Also: the intent-extra tests pinned protocol_version 1; records are v2
